Synopsis:
Mortach Scyre, Priestess of Kelemvor, is a kind and gentle older woman (who will also not hestitate to beat your ass). She can come across a little morbid, but that's simply because she is completely at peace with death in a way very few people are. She is like the shephard of the graveyard - guiding and offering help where needs be.In this dialogue, she reacts to the things you've done to help people around the graveyard (and also to chastise you in the case of Nina, if you help her raise her brother from the dead)

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_KelemvorPriestess.json: The exchange takes place in the graveyard under Mortarch Gracie Scyre’s care; she is a gentle, older priestess of Kelemvor who speaks plainly about death and acts as the cemetery’s shepherd. Off‑screen, the player has been intervening in mourners’ affairs — sometimes helping them, and in at least one case (Nina) using or teaching necromancy to raise a loved one — which provokes Mortarch’s quiet fury. While she calmly offers comfort, teachings, and blessings to those who accept death, she will condemn and expel anyone who uses necromancy to manipulate the grieving or harm innocents, invoking Kelemvor’s judgment. Other city conflicts (Bhaal cult activity, Orin, etc.) may be happening elsewhere but do not change her focus on protecting these hallowed grounds.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_PriestessAndNecromancer.json: Scyre, Mortach of Kelemvor, has been told that a little girl is practicing Necromancy in the graveyard. This is when you catch up to them both, and you get one last chance to intervene. In this dialogue you can encourage Nina to stop her Necromancy, threaten her, or even convince her to try again later.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_Gravekeeper.json: A weary gravekeeper, absolutely exhausted at having to bury so many bodies in recent days. Would be good to have her have typical gallows humour, but be relatively kindhearted and helpful underneath it (though relatively unimportant) She will exclusively hang around the gravekeeper's house, and likely either be found sat and resting or just idly milling around a small area.Important topics:- Where you can find a shovel- Killings in Baldur's Gate (with a branch for if it's solved)- (When you've encountered them) Kobold Looters- Something to chastise the player if they've gone around digging up graves themselves, probably a HasMet alt?
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_AD_NecromancerIdles.json: Nina Dortmell is a bereaved child who, despite her youth, wields unnerving necromantic power and enjoys the favor of Myrkul. Off‑screen her brother Garret is dead and she’s been trying to raise him, alternately furious and desperate when rituals fail and pleading at his grave when the player convinces her to let him rest. The lines reflect two likely states: a frantic, inexperienced caster puzzling over a failed resurrection (“Why won’t it work?! / I’m gonna save you Garret — I promise”) or a quieter, grieving child who has been persuaded to leave Garret in peace and now mourns him (“Come home, big brother — please”). Any failure is portrayed as emotional and practical frustration rather than an explanation — Nina lacks the answers for why her power won’t bring him back.
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_FatherCarrion.json: Dialog with Mystic Carrion, a mummy lord hiding in the Lower City. Players who carry the Necromancy of Thay (unread) have the chance to take part in a seance where they can learn how the book can be opened. Players can also take on a quest from Carrion, to bring back his runaway zombie beggar Thrumbo (potentially in exchange for the torch of revocation, intended to help Oskar).Various conclusions are available for the quest to help Mystic Carrion - if the player succeeds in bringing himThrumbo's torso, he will reward them with a Torch of revocation which can be used to cure Oskar's possession (Oskar's Beloved). If you refuse him, he will attack you, and keep returnign from the dead until you destroy his canopic jar (hidden inside Thrumbo)

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: Tell me, saer, if you leave a poisoned cake in a park and a child dies from eating said cake, are you responsible for the child's death? || [context] NodeContext: quietly furious (node 1)
- Player: In part. But the child's parents share the blame. (node 24)
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: Such wisdom. Which means you do not even have the excuse of ignorance. || [context] NodeContext: quietly furious (node 20)
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: You showed a grieving child the ways of necromancy. Leave these hallowed grounds now. May Kelemvor have mercy on your soul. || [context] NodeContext: disgusted (node 9)

Sample 2:
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: Tell me, saer, if you leave a poisoned cake in a park and a child dies from eating said cake, are you responsible for the child's death? || [context] NodeContext: quietly furious (node 1)
- Player: It is the fault of the gods for not intervening. (node 4)
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: I cannot believe you truly think that. || [context] NodeContext: quietly furious (node 2)
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: You showed a grieving child the ways of necromancy. Leave these hallowed grounds now. May Kelemvor have mercy on your soul. || [context] NodeContext: disgusted (node 9)

Sample 3:
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: Breathe it in - the damp. The decay. The smell is sweeter than roses - for death is a gift worth cherishing. (node 30)
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: How might I be of assistance? (node 15)
- Player: I'm good - thanks. (node 34)
- Mortarch Gracie Scyre: Fear not death, and He shall welcome you. (node 16)

context: The scene is set in the Kurwin graveyard under the care of Mortarch Gracie Scyre, a gentle, plain‑spoken priestess of Kelemvor who shepherds the dead and comforts mourners while being utterly at peace with death. Off‑screen the player has been meddling in graveside affairs—helping some mourners but in at least one case teaching or using necromancy to try to raise a bereaved child’s brother (Nina and Garret). Scyre quietly condemns any use of necromancy that manipulates the grieving or profanes the hallowed ground, offering comfort to those who accept death and expulsion and Kelemvor’s judgment to those who do not. Other city troubles may be happening elsewhere, but her focus here is protecting the cemetery and its mourners.
